_comment: DENY-SIDE BACKSTOP for the zebra vetting agents. Tracked in git.
Read this before adding anything to an 'allow' list here: measured on
2026-08-12, a project settings.json ALLOW rule is IGNORED by `claude -p`.
Claude Code will not grant itself permissions from a file sitting in its
working directory — otherwise cloning a repo would hand it capabilities.
DENY rules from this file ARE honoured.
So the grants live on the spawn command line instead: zebra/config.py
VET_ALLOWED_TOOLS -> `--allowedTools`, verified end-to-end by having a
real spawned agent run `zebra vet show` and return the right answer.
This file is the second layer, and it is the one that matters most: it
still applies when a human runs `claude` interactively on the Pi, where
THE INVARIANT: no agent, spawned or interactive, may open or close a
position. Verified 2026-08-12 by asking a real agent to run
`zebra close --help` (harmless even if the deny failed) — it answered
DENIED. Do not weaken these patterns; the wildcards are what make them
survive a `cd foo && python -m zebra close` phrasing.
